identity.title: CyberGym: Evaluating AI Agents' Real-World Cybersecurity Capabilities at Scale

problem.claim: Assess AI agents’ cybersecurity capabilities, including performance on dynamic, real-world security challenges.

gap.claim: Existing evaluations rely on small benchmarks and static outcomes, so they do not capture the full range of real-world security challenges.

contributions.claim: Introduces CyberGym, a large-scale benchmark containing 1,507 real-world vulnerabilities from 188 software projects.
Defines adjustable vulnerability-analysis settings, primarily asking agents to generate proof-of-concept tests reproducing vulnerabilities from textual descriptions and codebases.
Presents CyberGym as both a capability-measurement benchmark and a platform intended to produce direct real-world security impact.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish CyberGym from static, small-scale evaluations through its large-scale, real-world vulnerability suite, reproducibility task, and reported vulnerability-discovery outcomes.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that CyberGym differentiates the cybersecurity capabilities of agents and models.
The authors report that even the best-performing agent–model combinations achieve only about a 20% success rate, indicating substantial task difficulty.
The authors report discovery of 34 zero-day vulnerabilities and 18 historically incomplete patches beyond static benchmarking.

narrative_sequence.summary: AI agents may reshape cybersecurity, motivating comprehensive capability assessment.
Existing small-scale, static evaluations miss the dynamic breadth of real-world security challenges.
CyberGym addresses this with 1,507 vulnerabilities across 188 projects and a proof-of-concept reproduction task based on descriptions and codebases.
The authors report capability differentiation, roughly 20% peak success, and discoveries of zero-days and incomplete patches.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a benchmark-scale specification with a concrete task and reports both capability scores and real-world discoveries.

lessons.interpretation: This aligns what is being measured with an external-impact pathway, rather than relying on a single static score.
lessons.application: When presenting an evaluation resource, specify the task inputs and outputs, quantify its coverage, and report a downstream-impact signal alongside benchmark performance.
lessons.exception: This pattern may be unsuitable when downstream impact cannot be safely or credibly measured.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify evaluation participants, baselines, protocols, or statistical uncertainty for the reported success rate.
It does not explain how zero-day discoveries and incomplete patches were validated or attributed.
The scope and operational differences among the adjustable vulnerability-analysis settings are unspecified.
